# Vendored test fixtures

Two files, used only by `../md-spec.html`, which is served only when the daemon is started with
`-testdata testdata`. They are somebody else's documents, kept here so a conformance run reproduces
offline against a version that will not move under it. Nothing in this directory is compiled, embedded or
shipped: `//go:embed all:web` does not reach `testdata/`, and 140 KB of someone else's examples has no
business inside a binary.

Both documents carry the same licence, and it is not the permissive one people expect from a test suite.

## commonmark.0.31.2.json

    source   https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/spec.json
    fetched  2026-11-06
    size     140 487 bytes, 652 examples
    sha256   d431b29d97b6f73e69d547109cf5081578fac931e72afe95639ebe766c1b2a20
    licence  CC BY-SA 4.0 — https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

The CommonMark project's own machine-readable examples, from the document that says of itself:

> CommonMark Spec by John MacFarlane is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0
> International License. — https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/ (Version 0.31.2, 2024-01-28)

Each entry is `{markdown, html, example, start_line, end_line, section}`; `start_line`/`end_line` point
back into the spec document, which is what makes a failure readable. **The file is byte-identical to what
that URL returned on the fetch date** — check it with the checksum above rather than with this sentence.

markedjs/marked publishes a copy of the same data at `test/specs/commonmark/`, generated by fetching this
exact URL and adding a `shouldFail` flag to the examples marked itself does not pass. That copy is not
used here, for two reasons: one file with one licensor is easier to account for than one file with two,
and a conformance page that reads another renderer's annotations is a page that will eventually report
marked's result and call it ours.

## gfm.0.29.json

    source   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markedjs/marked/master/test/specs/gfm/gfm.0.29.json
    fetched  2026-11-06, marked master at ba50aa9 (v18.1.3)
    size     8 812 bytes, 28 examples
    sha256   586744ab8f12b35e6c6d4e351e49141540ed17bb3810195e71a5c505bb3b1729
    licence  CC BY-SA 4.0 for the examples, MIT for the transcription

The GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions — tables, task list items, strikethrough, autolinks — as examples.
Two documents stand behind this file and both are named because both are needed:

- The underlying work is the GFM specification, which says of itself “This formal specification is based
  on the CommonMark Spec by John MacFarlane and licensed under [CC BY-SA 4.0]”
  (https://github.github.com/gfm/, Version 0.29-gfm, 2019-04-06). Its source repository, `github/gfm`, no
  longer exists: the rendered document is the only form it is available in, which is a large part of why
  these fixtures are vendored at all instead of fetched at run time.
- The transcription into JSON is marked's `test/update-specs.js`, which scrapes that rendered page and
  keeps the example number the document itself assigns, a `section` label it invents, and the markdown and
  html with surrounding whitespace trimmed; it also flags with `shouldFail` the examples marked does not
  pass. marked is MIT, “Copyright (c) 2018+, MarkedJS … Copyright (c) 2011-2018, Christopher Jeffrey”
  (https://github.com/markedjs/marked/blob/master/LICENSE). The examples are the spec's, not marked's.

## What that licence asks of this repository

Named plainly, because “we copied a test file” is not a thing to rediscover in three years:

- **Attribution** is what this file is. If it is moved, moved with it.
- **Indicate changes**: there are none. Re-running the checksums above is the proof; editing an example,
  deleting one, or reformatting a file makes the result an adaptation, and an adaptation is still CC BY-SA.
- **ShareAlike** reaches the fixtures and anything derived from them. It does not reach `web/js/md.js`:
  that renderer was written against the prose and does not contain a line of these files, and testing an
  implementation against a document is not making a derivative of it. Anyone who doubts that sentence
  should read the licence, not this file.
- These terms belong to these two files whatever else this repository is licensed under. As of this
  writing the repository carries no LICENSE file of its own at all — that is a separate question, and not
  one these two files create.

## Refreshing

Both files are version-pinned by name, so an update means adding a file and deciding whether to keep the
old one — not silently changing the ground under a comparison:

    cd testdata/md
    curl -sfLO https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/spec.json && mv spec.json commonmark.0.31.2.json
    curl -sfLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/markedjs/marked/master/test/specs/gfm/gfm.0.29.json
    sha256sum commonmark.0.31.2.json gfm.0.29.json

Update the checksums and the fetch date above in the same commit, and `md-spec.html`'s `SUITES` list if the
version in the filename changed.
